    gg = np.where(g > 0, g, 1)
    div = (t % gg) == 0
    return m(sel & div) - m(sel & ~div)'
w interval_inside_vs_outside_near "In size>=2 sets, yes rate for unshown targets strictly inside [min,max] minus targets outside the range within 1-10 of nearest example; observed above null means the model under-weights interval/range-based generalisation." '    sel = n >= 2

    return m(far & (n >= 3)) - m(far & (n == 1))'
w between_set_yes_rate_spread "Standard deviation across distinct number_sets of the per-set yes rate; observed above null means sets differ more in overall endorsement (rule vs similarity sets) than the model predicts." '    s = pd.Series(r).groupby(df["number_set"].astype(str).to_numpy()).mean()
    v = float(s.std(ddof=0)) if len(s) > 1 else 0.0
    return v if np.isfinite(v) else 0.0'
w trial_index_drift "Correlation between trial_index and yes response; observed differing from null means response bias drifts over the session in a way the model does not capture." '    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy()

# name: parity_rule_contrast
# description: In all-even sets of size>=2, yes rate for even minus odd targets at distance>10 from every example; observed above null means the model under-produces parity-rule generalisation.
def test_statistic(df):
    S = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(S), axis=1)
    Si = np.nan_to_num(S, nan=0.0).astype(int)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(S - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    smin = np.nanmin(S, axis=1); smax = np.nanmax(S, axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(np.mean(r[mask])) if np.sum(mask) > 0 else 0.0
    ev = (n >= 2) & np.all((Si % 2 == 0) | np.isnan(S), axis=1)
    far = dist > 10
    return m(ev & far & (t % 2 == 0)) - m(ev & far & (t % 2 == 1))

content.text:
I wrote all 8 test statistics to `iter_1/critique/test_stats/`. Last attempt's files were rejected for importing pandas; these import nothing and use only the `np` and `pd` the harness already provides. I ran each one once on the observed responses (2,520 rows): all returned a finite number in about 0.02 s or less, well under the 0.3 s per-call budget. I did not run the posterior-predictive harness or the model; the pipeline does that.

They target what a summed-similarity model (distance plus final digit) should get wrong. "Far" means at least that distance from every example, and "unshown" means the target isn't one of the examples.

| Statistic | What it measures | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `target_in_set_yes_rate` | Yes rate when the target is one of the examples | 0.70 |
| `parity_rule_contrast` | All-even sets: yes rate for even minus odd targets, far (>10) | 0.29 |
| `power_of_two_contrast` | Powers-of-two sets: unshown power-of-two targets minus other even targets | 0.48 |
| `common_divisor_rule_contrast` | Sets with a common divisor ≥3 (not 10): divisible minus non-divisible targets, distance >5 | −0.02 |
| `interval_inside_vs_outside_near` | Unshown targets inside the set's range minus targets 1–10 outside it | 0.07 |
| `set_size_effect_far_targets` | Yes rate for far targets (>20): sets of 3+ minus single-example sets | −0.11 |
| `between_set_yes_rate_spread` | Spread (SD) of the yes rate across sets | 0.23 |
| `trial_index_drift` | Correlation between trial position and answering yes | 0.03 |

Each file's description says which direction counts as the model getting it wrong. For example, a parity or powers-of-two contrast above the model's prediction means it is missing rule-like generalisation. Whether any of these is a significant discrepancy will only be known once the pipeline computes the p-values.
